items.line: δρογύνης ibid.). — Das castrirte Geschöpf (§. 20) heißt סרים (ibid.
items.note: The castrated being in rabbinic Hebrew is סריס (saris, 'eunuch'), discussed in Bechoroth. סרים is not a word with this meaning; the final ם is a misread of ס.

items.line: Küchlein רצוצא (ibid. 8, b), das noch nicht flüggegewordene Junge
items.note: Reading A, רצוצא, is the Aramaic term from Bechoroth 8b for an unhatched chick, matching Lewysohn's 'noch nicht ausgekrochene Küchlein'. Reading B, רעצא, is not an attested word.

items.line: אפרוח**) (Beza 4, a), das schon etwas ältergewordene Junge: גוזל***). —
items.note: The young bird is standardly spelled גוזל, as in Gen 15:9 and in rabbinic usage. The defective spelling גזל is possible in print but would normally mean 'robbery'.

items.line: בת vor dem eigentlichen Thiernamen, z. B. בן יונה, die junge Taube,
items.note: The text pairs בן with its feminine counterpart, and the example בת חמרא ('die junge Eselin') shows that counterpart is בת. The following 'Für בן…' likely introduces Aramaic בר separately.

items.line: בן חמור, der junge Esel, בת חמרא, die junge Eselin u. s. w. Für בן
items.note: The gloss 'die junge Eselin' is feminine, and the preceding line names בן or בת as the prefixes, so the word is בת. בר is the masculine Aramaic form.

items.line: ten סרים אדם, von dem unfruchtbar geborenen Menschen סרים חמה. — Das
items.note: The Talmud's terms are סריס אדם (a eunuch made by man) and סריס חמה (one born sterile), at Yevamot 79b. The word is סריס; סרים is a misread of the final ס as final ם.

items.line: ten סרים אדם, von dem unfruchtbar geborenen Menschen סרים חמה. — Das
items.note: The Talmudic terms in Jebamoth 79b are סריס אדם (a eunuch made by man) and סריס חמה (a congenital eunuch). סרים, with final mem, is an OCR confusion of ם for ס and is not the word.

items.line: אנפת) die Bezeichnung גוזרים für saugende Kinder.
items.note: The passage is about extended uses of גוזל (young bird), so the paytan's term for nursing children is probably a related form. גוזרים fits that pattern (possibly a garbled גוזלים); גורים ('whelps') would not illustrate גוזל.

items.line: aufrechten Stellung מהלך שתים „Zweifüßler“ (Keritot 21, b), wäh-
items.note: The Talmudic phrase (Keritot 21b) is spelled defectively, מהלך (על) שתים. The plene spelling שתיים is a modern orthography unlikely in an 1858 print.

items.line: Falle heißen sämmtliche zu essen gestattete (größeren) Säugethiere חיותא
items.note: חיותא is the standard Aramaic word for 'animal/beast', which fits the generic term for edible mammals cited from Meïle 20b. חיוהא is not a word; the ת was misread as ה.

items.line: tung, z. B. בר אווא (Ente §. 244), בת יענה (Strauß §. 240), בר יוכני (§. 502),
items.note: Both readings appear in this line: בר אווא glossed 'Ente' (§. 244) and בר יוכני (§. 502), the legendary giant bird. The readings are too different to be a look-alike letter error, so it is unclear which slot is in question. I am guessing it is the first, the duck.

items.line: tung, z. B. בר אווא (Ente §. 244), בת יענה (Strauß §. 240), בר יוכני (§. 502),
items.note: בר יוכני is the well-known mythical giant bird of Bekhorot 57b, which fits the §. 502 reference. אוזא looks like a garbled form of אווזא (duck, the separate §. 244 entry). It is unclear which slot the variant belongs to.

items.line: בר נפחא (§. 217), בר חיריא (§. 192) u. a. m.
items.note: בר חיריא fits the Aramaic root חרא ('dung'), likely an animal name; היריא gives no known word. Not verified against the source.

items.line: Die Vögel nennt der Talmud nicht מהלכי שתים und wohl mit Recht,
items.note: The Talmudic phrase for 'two-legged walkers' is standardly spelled מהלכי שתים, and an 1858 print would likely use the defective spelling. The plene שתיים is a valid variant, though, so both readings are possible.

items.line: wo der durch den Flug angerichtete Schaden als תולדה דרגל angesehen wird.
items.note: The standard Talmudic term is 'תולדה דרגל' (Bava Kamma 2b), meaning a derivative of the 'foot' category of damages. 'דהרגל' is not the usual form.

items.line: unterschied man in Betreff des Aufenthalts ביתיות „im Hause le-
items.note: Beza 40a contrasts plural forms, ביתיות and מדבריות. The paired word here is the plural מדבריות, so ביתיות matches it.

items.line: lebenden Thiere (wie das auswärts lebende Vieh §. 3) חיואי ברייתי***)
items.note: Aramaic בָּרָיְתָא means 'outside/wild', with plural ברייתי; חיואי ברייתי = 'outdoor (wild) animals'. The other reading, בריותי, would mean 'creatures' and does not fit 'auswärts lebend'.

items.line: שביהודה גדילה על פירות שבגליל ואין חיה שבגליל גדילה על פירות שביהודה

items.line: שביהודה גדילה על פירות שבגליל ואין חיה שבגליל גדילה על פירות שביהודה
items.note: Pesachim 52b reads אין חיה שביהודה גדילה על פירות שבגליל, where גדילה means 'raised/nourished on', which fits the German gloss about the animal's sustenance. גרילה is not a word.

items.line: auch ריחשא (Sabbat 146, b). Uneigentlich werden Feldthiere ערודי
items.note: ערוד (wild ass, pl. ערודי) is the Aramaic used loosely for field animals in B. Batra 36a, likely ‘ארעא דאכלוה ערודי’; ערהי is not a recognizable word here.

items.note: ליתני ('let it teach') is a standard Tosafot dibbur ha-matḥil heading, here Tos. Nidda 23. ליוחני is not a word; the OCR likely misread ת as וח.

items.line: רמש על הארץ sind Helminthen und die aus Verwesung fremder Sub-
items.note: The parallel 'שורץ על הארץ' and Lev 11:44 'הרומש על הארץ', which Maimonides draws on, favour the participle רומש. The noun רמש is still possible, so this is not certain.

items.note: Aboth 3:1 reads "למקום עפר רמה ותולעה", so the generic word for worm is תולע/תולעה. הולע is not a word; the ת was misread as ה.

items.line: Im jerusalem. Talm. bezeichnet דגה jedoch nur die kleine Fischart כולכיד,
items.note: The -ית ending fits a Hebrew noun for a small fish. כולכיד is not a recognizable word form, but I could not verify the exact spelling in the Yerushalmi (Nedarim).

items.note: 'מנהג אשכנז' is the standard phrase for the German rite, glossing 'deutschen Ritus'. 'אשכנזי' is grammatically possible but less idiomatic, so this leans on usage rather than certainty.

items.line: הארץ וכלם יראים מפני (Frankel's Monatsschrift 6, Jahrg. S. 271).
items.note: The sense is 'all fear Him', so the expected form is מפניו. מפני is a real word and the closer misreading, likely with a dropped final ו. מפונו is not a word.

items.line: richtigungen bedarf. Sie lautet: כל המוליד מניק וכל חמטיל בצים
items.note: The phrase in Bekhorot 7b is כל המטיל ביצים, and it parallels כל המוליד earlier in the sentence. המטיל means 'the one that lays eggs'; חמטיל is not a word.

items.line: heißt es: הרנגולת לכ״א יום „die Henne zu 21 Tagen“. Raschi erklärt:
items.note: The Hebrew word for hen is תרנגולת, so הרנגולת is a ח/ת-type misreading of the initial letter. The gershayim in לכ"א (21 days, matching "zu 21 Tagen") is also preserved in B.

items.line: חמום התרנגולת אותה שלשה שבועות
items.note: The phrase means 'the warmth (brooding) of the hen,' and the Hebrew for hen is התרנגולת. Reading B, החרנגולת, is not a word; it is an OCR confusion of ת with ח.

items.line: den Dotter (חלמון**), R.: מויל, moyeu), bei den unreinen Vögeln
items.note: Rashi's Old French gloss for the yolk is moyeul, written מויל with a vav, and the passage line itself shows מויל. The second word (חנא vs תנא) is uncertain; תנא is the commoner Talmudic word, which weakens A.

items.line: dung ist die Bildung der Blase (שילפוחא, Raschi: ווישיאה, vessie);
items.note: Rashi's Old French gloss 'vessie' is conventionally spelled with a double vav for initial v, giving ווישיאה. ושיאה lacks the v-sound and the vowel yod, but a shortened print spelling can't be ruled out.

items.note: פטפט 'chatter, twitter' is the reduplicated root used of birds (Arachin 16b, of the sparrow). פטפש is not a word; final ש is an OCR misreading of ט.

items.note: B. Kama 60b uses the verbs בוכים and משחקים, and the parallel root form בכה suggests the root שחק; but the gloss „Gelächter“ could equally fit the noun שחוק.

items.note: The cricket name (rabbinic צרצור, from the chirping root צרר) is most likely written plene as צירצור (tzirtzur); B's ו may be a misread י, but this is uncertain.

items.line: geis war schon früh bekannt, was schon aus seinem Namen אנדרפטא,

items.line: allerersten Jugend עגל הרך, dann עגל, später עגלת בקר, עגלא תילתא
items.note: The Talmudic term is עגלא תילתא, the "third-grown calf" (Shabbat 11a, Sanhedrin 65b). הילתא is not a word in this sense; ה is a common misreading of ת.

items.note: My recollection of the Talmud's Aramaic for crustacean feelers (Shabbat 77b) is roughly 'קרני סילוא', which fits סילו. I can't fully confirm this, and סולו is not clearly ruled out.

items.line: Fliege: טיפין (Nidda 25, a). — Die Augenwimpern: תימורא (Sab-
items.note: The passage itself prints ריס של עין (eyelash), so ריס is right and רים is a ס/ם confusion. תימורא matches the Shabbat 77b term for eyelashes, so חימורא looks like a ת/ח misread.

items.note: Bechoroth 38b explains ריס as תורא בראה דעינא, 'the outer row/rim of the eye', with תורא meaning 'row'; חורא ('hole/white') does not fit. Recalled from memory, not checked.

items.line: Die Scheidewand und die beiden äußeren Wände der Nase: חוטמין
items.note: Lewysohn spells the singular plene as חוטם in the line above, so the plural חוטמין fits his usage. The defective חטמין is also a possible spelling, so this is not certain.

items.line: der innern durchlöcherten Nasenwand trägt, heißt חטם (Sabbat 5, 1).
items.note: Mishnah Shabbat 5:1 reads 'נאקה בחטם', the nose-ring worn through the pierced nasal septum, matching the German description. The next line also derives חרטום from חוטם. חסם means 'muzzle', which does not fit.

items.line: Nach Raschi (B. Kama 55, a) heißt der Schnabel auch קיע. — Das
items.note: B. Kama 55a uses קועיה for the beak (Rashi glosses it as חרטום), so the printed word is probably קוע. Reading A differs from that only by the common ו/י confusion, while B עוק would need the letters reversed.

items.note: I could not verify the cited Bekhorot 44a passage. חוורות is feminine and could agree with the ears (feminine); חתומי is a masculine construct and fits less well. This is a guess.

items.note: Garbled Old French gloss in Rashi; Lewysohn's dor/bosse reading does not fix the first letter. ח is a slightly likelier guess, but ה is equally plausible.

items.note: Both spell the same word ('two', for walking on two feet). The defective spelling שתים is the standard rabbinic and 19th-century print form; the plene שתיים is more modern, so A is the likely printed reading.

items.note: This follows the parallel structure of the passage: the next line has קפץ התחתון for the lower joint and gives ערקוב as the generic name for both. So קפץ העליונה most likely names the upper joint. The feminine העליונה would fit an ארכובה-type noun better, so this is uncertain.

items.note: The marked line already prints ערקוב as the general name for both joints, and ערקוב is the Aramaic for the hock (cf. ארכובה) in the Bechoroth passage. The two readings are not look-alike letter variants, so it is unclear which word the engines disagreed on; this is a guess.

items.line: bien. — יארוד (Sanhedrin 59, b) Raschi als Vogel, Andere als
items.note: Reading A gives three real words that fit their sources. יארוד is the Sanhedrin 59b creature that Rashi explains as a bird. תוא is the biblical animal that Kimchi takes as an aurochs. ברבורים is from 1 Kings 5:3. Reading B's יארור and תיא are not words.
